**Release candidate.** v0.1.0-rc.2 is accepted for the documented beta/RC deployment envelope only. It is not a claim of general production readiness or of fleet capacity.

## Scope and restrictions

- **Fixes the v0.1.0-rc.1 known defect (unbounded memory growth under MySQL table-ID churn).** A MySQL source now holds the binlog table maps of the open transaction only, in its binlog parser and in its own state, and releases them at each transaction end and when the stream is reopened; table maps of excluded tables are released the same way. A rows event without a table map in its transaction now stops the source fail-closed instead of being skipped. On the workload that OOM-killed v0.1.0-rc.1 (100,000 tables, 40,000 receiving writes, 6 GiB limit), DeltaForge's memory stayed near 810 MiB for 35 minutes with no missing, duplicate or out-of-order change; that run is a memory and correctness check, not a throughput result. **v0.1.0-rc.1 images remain affected; upgrade.**
- **Trusted, isolated networks only.** There is no transport encryption to source databases, a PostgreSQL state store, or Kafka and Redis sinks; Kafka SASL `PLAIN` sends credentials in clear; the REST API and metrics are unauthenticated. Not suitable where transport encryption is required.
- **Single instance, qualified scope only.** Qualification covered one MySQL 8.4 server with 40,000 tables and one pipeline, and one PostgreSQL 17 source with 1,000 tables, both on the SQLite state store; the table-map fix was also checked at 100,000 tables with 40,000 receiving writes, for memory and correctness only. Larger catalogs, dense active sets and fleets are not qualified, and multi-pipeline capacity is unqualified: there is no fleet-capacity qualification. Capacity guidance is a starting point, not a tested ceiling.
- **Not validated:** source versions other than PostgreSQL 17 and MySQL 8.4 (MySQL 8.0.19 is the minimum; MariaDB is refused), managed database services, the PostgreSQL state store, live credential rotation and dynamic Vault credentials, and sink versions other than those the release gate runs.
- **Operational limits:** delivery is at-least-once (consumers deduplicate on the event `id`); a pipeline that stops fail-closed stays stopped until an operator restarts it; preflight does not cover every startup requirement; back up the SQLite state store with the documented WAL-safe procedure.
- **Upgrade step:** a source with retained state from an earlier release is refused until it is adopted once with `deltaforge state-binding adopt`.
- **Open incident I1:** one unexplained SIGBUS of the `sources` library test binary in a CI coverage run (at `df726153`). It passed on rerun and on every later revision. Unresolved and non-blocking; any recurrence blocks release.

See the [Supported Deployment Envelope](https://vnvo.github.io/deltaforge/deployment-support.html) and the [Release Checklist](https://github.com/vnvo/deltaforge/blob/v0.1.0-rc.2/docs/ops/release-checklist.md).

## Platforms

The tagged commit is the release commit the release checks tested.

- **`linux/amd64`:** the release checks built and smoke-tested the minimal and debug images from the release commit on amd64, and every test suite and qualification ran on amd64. The published images are built by the release workflow from the tagged commit.
- **`linux/arm64`:** built by the release workflow from the tagged commit. Not covered by the release checks or by qualification: not validated.
